pull_request_body: This issue measures the cost of coverage and branch measurement on the CI test job. It runs four configurations (no coverage, lines, lines+branches, lines+ctrace) three times each on an idle host, records CPU and wall time, and times the serial coverage commands separately. The result is a table in the pull request that states the cost of branch measurement in seconds. If the numbers show a large share in the report or combine step, a CI option change follows. No threshold is lowered.
why: The owner asked on 2026-10-27 (the decision comment on #2356) whether measuring branches is worth its job time, as #2163 proposes. No clean number exists for what coverage costs the test job. Previous attempts were confounded by host load or changed three variables at once. #2373 measures the cost on a quiet host and reports it on #2163.
what_changes: Run four coverage configurations (no coverage, lines, lines+branches, lines+ctrace) three times each on an idle host and record median CPU and wall time
Time the serial coverage commands (combine, report, xml) separately on the data of the lines run
State the cost of branch measurement in seconds of CPU and job time
If the report or combine step is a large share, test lower-cost --cov-report options without lowering any threshold
feasibility: The premise is confirmed by openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-27-2356-coverage-floor-and-test-cost/design.md section 4, which states: 'The cost of branch measurement is not established. The owner asked for it.' and names #2373 as the issue that measures it.

The same design.md records the gate command (pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml), the 16-worker parallel setup, the 287 s gate time, and the failed same-day comparison (load average 10 to 39).
The 568 s ctrace run changed three variables at once (core, contexts, branches), so it does not isolate the cost of branches.

First checks the implementation runs: (1) uptime to confirm the host is idle (load under 2); (2) uv run pytest --collect-only -q to confirm the suite collects; (3) uv run coverage --version to confirm coverage.py is installed; (4) uv run pytest tests/test_cli_startup_imports.py --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing to confirm the coverage plugin loads.
existing_tool: coverage.py (with pytest-cov) is already in use. The sysmon and ctrace cores, branch measurement, and the combine/report/xml commands are options of coverage.py. Nothing new is built.

decisions.decision: Run the benchmark on a local idle host rather than in CI
decisions.reason: The issue requires uptime under 2 before each run. CI runners are shared and cannot guarantee an idle host. A local host gives a clean number.

decisions.decision: Use the median of three runs rather than the mean
decisions.reason: The median is robust to one outlier run. The issue names the median as the reported figure.

decisions.decision: Time the serial commands separately after the parallel run
decisions.reason: The parallel run hides the cost of combine, report, and xml. Timing them alone isolates the serial tail that the issue asks about.

decisions.decision: Include a spec delta on ci-coverage-reports
decisions.reason: The change potentially alters the --cov-report options of the test job, which is an observable devops command option. The rules state that a devops command option change carries a spec delta.

rejected.alternative: Run the benchmark in a CI job
rejected.evidence: The issue requires uptime under 2 before each run. CI runners are shared and the 2026-10-27 attempt failed because the load average was 10 to 39 from other runs (design.md section 4).

rejected.alternative: Use the 568 s ctrace run as the branch cost
rejected.evidence: The design.md states: 'Run 2 above took 568 s against 287 s, but it changes the ctrace core, the contexts and the branches together.' Three variables changed at once, so the number does not isolate the cost of branches.

rejected.alternative: Add a recurring CI job for this measurement
rejected.evidence: The issue states: 'It is a one-time benchmark. The result is a table in the pull request description. No recurring job is added.' (proposed design, key questions).

added.name: coverage-cost-benchmark-record
added.text: The change SHALL record the median CPU time and wall time of four coverage configurations (no coverage, lines, lines and branches, lines with ctrace core), each from three runs on a host with uptime under 2, and SHALL state the cost of branch measurement in seconds of CPU time and job time.

scenarios.name: benchmark table complete
scenarios.when: the three runs of each configuration complete on a host with uptime under 2
scenarios.then: the results document contains a table with four rows, each showing the median user-plus-system CPU time and wall time

scenarios.name: branch cost stated in seconds
scenarios.when: the medians of the lines and lines-and-branches configurations are computed
scenarios.then: the results document states the difference in seconds of CPU time and job time

added.name: coverage-report-options-cost
added.text: When the report or combine step is a large share of the lines configuration CPU time, the test job SHALL use coverage report options that reduce CPU time without lowering any coverage threshold.

scenarios.name: report option reduced without threshold change
scenarios.when: the report step is a large share of the lines configuration CPU time
scenarios.then: the test job drops the term-missing report from the runner and the coverage floor value in pyproject.toml is unchanged

groups.title: Run four coverage configurations and record medians
groups.test: Write a check that benchmark-results.md contains four configuration rows (no coverage, lines, lines and branches, lines with ctrace core), each with three runs of user-plus-system CPU time and wall time, and a median column. The file does not exist, so the check fails
groups.implementation: Check uptime is under 2. For each of the four configurations, run uv run pytest with the gate options three times. Record user-plus-system CPU time and wall time for each run. Compute the median. Write the table to benchmark-results.md

groups.title: Time the serial coverage commands
groups.test: Write a check that benchmark-results.md contains a section with separate timings for coverage combine, coverage report --show-missing, and coverage xml, each with CPU and wall time. The section does not exist, so the check fails
groups.implementation: Using the .coverage data files from the lines run, run coverage combine, coverage report --show-missing, and coverage xml each alone. Record the CPU and wall time of each. Append the results to benchmark-results.md
groups.verify: grep -q 'coverage combine' openspec/changes/2373-coverage-cost-measurement/benchmark-results.md && grep -q 'coverage report' openspec/changes/2373-coverage-cost-measurement/benchmark-results.md && grep -q 'coverage xml' openspec/changes/2373-coverage-cost-measurement/benchmark-results.md

groups.title: State the cost and apply the conditional change
groups.test: Write a check that design.md states the cost of branch measurement in seconds of CPU time and job time, and if the report step is a large share, that the CI option change is recorded with the threshold unchanged. The file does not exist, so the check fails
groups.implementation: Compute the difference between the lines and lines-and-branches medians. Write the cost in seconds of CPU and job time. If the report or combine step is a large share, record the lower-cost option and verify the coverage floor in pyproject.toml is unchanged. State that no threshold is lowered
